how: Read-only. A copy of /Applications/Grok Bot.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar was unpacked into the scratchpad with `npx @electron/asar` and searched; the app was not started, changed or messaged. In ~/Library/Application Support/Grok Bot/ only file names, sizes, dates, JSON key names and word COUNTS were read. No cookie, token, secret file or conversation text was opened, printed or copied.

app.where_the_agent_works: On Grok Bot's own cloud computer, not on this Mac. The app text says "Runs on Grok Bot's computer" and "Run a command on Grok Bot's computer"; the code speaks of a gateway, a pod and a remote screen (VNC) preview. That is the "own browser" Alan sees.

1_deep_links.found: grokbot://app/v1/<route> (sand:// is the same; https://cursor.com/grok-bot/link/... is the web form). At most 2,048 characters.

routes.sidebar?agent=&tab=&automation=&target=: open an agent's side panel on a tab (overview, routines, media, computer, meetings, members), optionally on one routine and on its webhook URL / webhook key / Authorization header field
routes.open: bring the app to the front
routes.marketplace, plugin-add, bot-template, c: browse or add plugins and templates

1_deep_links.why: No route has a text, prompt, message or file parameter. Every parameter is an id or a fixed word, checked against a pattern. A deep link navigates; it never speaks.

2_local_server_cli_mcp_watched_folder.local_server: None for commands. The only listeners in the code are a short-lived one for the sign-in return and a loopback one that feeds the app its own update.
2_local_server_cli_mcp_watched_folder.cli: None. Nothing named grokbot, grok-bot or sand is on the PATH; the bundle holds one executable and a 'Computer Use' helper app.
2_local_server_cli_mcp_watched_folder.mcp: The app is an MCP client, not a server: it can be GIVEN MCP servers ("Add a custom MCP server or secret for everyone using this Bot", "MCP server JSON"), which then load on Grok Bot's computer. It exposes none for us to call.
what_does_exist: ROUTINES WITH A WEBHOOK TRIGGER. The app has a trigger "When a webhook fires" and shows, per routine, a Webhook URL, a Webhook key and the line "Senders authenticate with this key: include an Authorization: Bearer <key> header in the webhook request". A routine is created by asking the bot in its chat ("Routines are recurring tasks this Bot runs on a schedule. Ask it in chat to set one up."). This is a real machine channel INTO the bot. What the request body may carry is decided on xAI's side and was not verifiable from the app.

CODE-HOST CONNECTIONS (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps) with triggers such as pr-opened and ci-failed: the bot can read and write a repository it is connected to. Whether Alan's bot is connected to our GitHub was not checked (that is account state).

LOCAL COMMANDS, behind a switch: "Allow Grok Bot and all Bots to run commands on your local computer?". With it on, the bot could write a file on this Mac. Its state was not read. Not recommended as a channel: it gives every bot a shell on the MacBook.
ATTACH FILES and DOWNLOAD FILE in the chat window: the human path.

3_where_transcripts_and_outputs_live.on_this_mac: ~/Library/Application Support/Grok Bot/sand-client-persistence/ : 13 small JSON files whose names are base32 of a key. Three are conversation copies (key ...transcript.replicas.<uuid>): 252,649 bytes / 148 entries (3 Oct 20:30Z to 4 Oct 04:54Z), 187,844 bytes / 135 entries (6 Sep to 3 Oct), 2,531 bytes / 3 entries. Entry keys: kind, id, role, content, timestampMs, seq. The whole folder is under half a megabyte.
3_where_transcripts_and_outputs_live.is_the_finbert_session_there: Yes: the 148-entry conversation holds the word finbert 64 times, sentiment 127 times and scintilla 107 times (counts only; the text was not read).
3_where_transcripts_and_outputs_live.is_the_captured_x_feed_there: No. That conversation holds 0 links of the form /status/ and 2 mentions of x.com. The posts the bot captured are on its cloud computer, not in these files.
3_where_transcripts_and_outputs_live.why_not: The local files are the app's private cache of chat text: no posts, no stable format promise (they carry a schemaVersion the app may change), and reading Alan's conversations is not a data feed.

the_channel_in_one_line: TODAY: HUMAN ONLY. Nothing can reach the bot from our side until a person types (or pastes) into its window once. AFTER ONE PASTE BY ALAN it can be machine-to-machine: a webhook in, a Git branch out.

setup_once_by_a_person: Alan opens the Test Bot conversation (a deep link can do the opening: grokbot://app/v1/agent?id=<its id>) and pastes DISPATCH-0 below.

The bot creates a routine with a webhook trigger. Alan copies its Webhook URL and Webhook key to the coordinator once; the key is stored as a Fly secret (keys-on-Fly rule) and is never written to a file or a page.
Alan confirms in the bot's Settings that the bot's GitHub connection reaches one repository we name for this purpose only.

dispatch_what_we_send.transport: HTTPS POST to the routine's Webhook URL with Authorization: Bearer <key>, sent from Fly. Until the webhook exists: the same text pasted by Alan.

DISPATCH-0_xfeed_job_spec.source: X list 1405188850188759047 (the Trading list the dead collector read), newest first
DISPATCH-0_xfeed_job_spec.cadence: every 2 hours 06:30 to 23:30 New York time (the collector's own schedule)
per_post_fields: original{ id, handle, created_at, text, url } for reposts and quotes
rules: read only: never like, reply, follow or post
never the X API, never export cookies
one file per pass, even when empty (an empty pass is a fact, not a failure)
no post older than the previous file's newest id, except in the first catch-up file

DISPATCH-1_finbert_bakeoff.input: deliverables/20261005/m1-models/bakeoff/x-short-text.json : the 300 posts and the rubric, WITHOUT the hand labels and model calls
DISPATCH-1_finbert_bakeoff.ask: score all 300 with the bot's FinBERT set-up exactly as it runs it today; state the model id and revision, the text cleaning, the label mapping and the threshold

return_what_it_sends_back.transport: one JSON file per pass committed to branch `grokbot/inbox` of the named repository, path xfeed/<UTC timestamp>.json or bakeoff/<job>.json. A Git commit is dated, signed by its account, replayable and reviewable; nothing of ours is exposed to the bot.
return_what_it_sends_back.return_line: STATUS · file path + commit · posts in file · newest post time · what was not captured and why

how_its_output_enters_our_tables: A job of ours (not the bot) reads new files on `grokbot/inbox`.
It refuses a file that fails the schema, has non-numeric ids, dates outside the last 10 days, or a newest id older than the last accepted one.
Accepted posts go through the existing scripts/xfeed-ingest.mjs path into the published feed (/api/xfeed), tagged source=grokbot, deduplicated on post id against what the collector already holds.
The existing sentiment-x-2h job then scores them into x_post_sentiment exactly as before. The bot never writes to a table and never holds a key of ours.
neighbours_this_touches: the restored MacBook collector (same feed: post ids must not double)
the heartbeat row for the X feed (two sources, one clock)
the keys-on-Fly rule (the webhook key is a new secret)
the no-paid rule: Grok Bot has Usage, Plan and On-demand settings, so its passes may be metered
proposed_protocol.pattern_followed: A Git branch as the hand-off point between two automated parties, with the receiving side validating before it ingests, is the pull-request model GitHub documents (https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests) and the 'inbox' pattern of ActivityPub (https://www.w3.org/TR/activitypub/#inbox).

not_verified: What a routine's webhook accepts in its body, and whether the body reaches the bot as its prompt (server side).
Whether Alan's bot is connected to GitHub, and whether local commands are switched on.
What the bot's X capture actually holds (it is on its cloud computer). The 0 '/status/' count says only that the posts are not in the local chat cache.
Whether a Grok Bot pass costs money beyond Alan's plan.
